P1.evidence: The setter read-back is the best example of P1a in the batch and did exactly what the check is for: "he briefed me in on your situation that you're 37, right? You're working in management mostly. You're standing right now... And you're training five, six a day on your own, doing, like, split plus cardio. Is that accurate?" Everything else in the phase was skipped. No four-part frame, no frame agreement, and no open question — he went straight from the read-back into baseline interrogation. The nearest thing arrives seven minutes later and is a tie-down, not an open question: "you came here for a reason, not just to have a chat. You want to fix this, right?"

P2.evidence: Eight of nine, and the strongest baseline anywhere in this batch. Age carried from the setter notes and confirmed; "how tall are you?" and "how much do you weigh?" both asked. Work and posture confirmed. Injuries asked directly and then probed intelligently for the sitting-related pattern — "I talk with a lot of guys that are sitting all day and they have back pain hip stiffness ankles" — which surfaced the morning lower-back stiffness. Training week established in detail down to the hour. Results challenged rather than accepted: "you weigh yourself that you feel that you lose the muscle?" Diet pushed past the generality — "if you could be more specific, what does it mean? Like, what do you eat exactly?" — through the entire day. Sleep asked and arithmetic done live to five or six hours. Energy asked twice and the afternoon nap unpicked. The single miss is the one that mattered most: health conditions were never asked, so two months of self-administered testosterone therapy only surfaced at 00:37:26 because the prospect volunteered it. Under the scoring rule that is a miss, and here it is a consequential one.

P3.evidence: The bridge ran clean — "my question is, what's your why? Why you want to do this?" — and was pushed when the first answer was surface: "What's changed between then and now?" The future question ran: "How do you feel after those six months, when you actually hit your goals and have this dream physique... how would you feel?" And the reflect-back is textbook: "So in a nutshell, it's not just about the number on the scale for you or the mirror. It's about walking into a room and feeling that you belong, that you're not behind. Is that a fair assessment?" → "Yeah, yeah." Worth crediting separately: the rep explicitly named and legitimised a confidence-and-partner why rather than forcing a longevity frame — "not everybody's here for the longevity and so on, that's totally okay, if that is your real and strong why" — which is what unlocked the honest answer. Missing: the mobility/strength/energy menu, the can't-do-now question, and the who-else-does-this-impact question. The identity layer was reached but the prospect supplied it.

P4.evidence: No past-attempts inventory at all — he was never asked what he has tried or what happened with it, which is a real gap for someone who has been training six days a week for years without the result. The root cause was asserted by the rep rather than elicited: "here's what I'm noticing, because you got the discipline, most people don't have that, what I'm not hearing is a program with actual logic to it" and "the biggest issue is of not being consistent, of falling off, of being on and off." The prospect did name the gap, but in answer to the why question rather than a P4 question — "I need the right people to guide me through and give me all the good things so I can just focus." The strongest move in the phase is a good variant of P4f applied to nutrition: "we won't do that with just pure willpower. Unfortunately, it doesn't work like that... You need a structure around your nutrition."

P5.evidence: Not run. No two-year question, no settling question, no why-not, no line in the sand. The closest fragment is "We're not here to be just complacent in where we are." This is the fourth consecutive call from this rep in this batch with no consequence frame — a settled pattern rather than an oversight, and the phase carries a weight of 20.

P6.evidence: The all-in question ran before the presentation, correctly placed and properly stress-tested: "the most important thing is, are you going to be fully committed to actually showing up and doing the work?" → "Yeah, 100%" → "Even when it's going to get tough. And it's going to get tough." → "Of course." The belief question also ran and ran well, but out of position — after the price, as an objection-handling move: "do you feel that can actually get you to leaner body, to have that big body and make you more confident and finally hit your goals?" P6c fails on the second clause: when hesitation surfaced, the script says return to Phase 5, and there was no Phase 5 to return to, so the rep went to finances and then to pressure instead.

P11.evidence: No payment was taken and the call ended with a follow-up booked for 9 July. Nothing in the phase was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: The most complete OA run in the batch. Four of the seven scripted moves ran, several near-verbatim: "do you feel that can actually get you to leaner body, to have that big body and make you more confident and finally hit your goals?", then "What makes you feel it can?", then "what's actually coming up for you right now that's preventing you from getting started?", then "you've been probably thinking about this for months now. So thinking, thinking is not the problem. Deciding is." Not run: the "the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision?" move, the identity move ("that man you want to be — how does HE decide right now?"), and the closing "Are you sure? Nothing else keeping you from being 100% in?" Scored on execution, not outcome — the play ran through and the prospect still declined.

The only complete financial picture in this batch. Isolation ran as a diagnostic question — "am I feeling correctly that this is not about thinking, but it's just a money thing right now?" The upfront norm ran with its rationale: "most of the guys that we work with take it up front and put it on a credit card... they are keeping themselves also accountable." The no-tough-spot framing and the custom-plan line ran as coached: "we don't have set payment plans. We do them, but we work with the client, whatever he's comfortable at that given moment." The permission question ran: "would you be comfortable having just an open conversation about the finances?" Then five of the six financial-picture items were actually asked — monthly surplus after bills ($2,500), savings (five-figure), investments and crypto (none), whether he has credit cards, and how much is left on them. Only the per-card available-credit total and the used-versus-available split were skipped. He then escalated off-call for terms and returned with two structures. Textbook, and it still did not close — which is the point of scoring process separately.

"I have vacation planned. So it's like more money to spend", restated later as "when I go on my vacation, because I told you I'm going on vacation tomorrow." The rep ran a priority reframe and a version of the recurring-obstacle move — "vacation is going to be next year, two years after, and so on" — which is the Thanksgiving line in different clothes. Not run: "things never slow down, when does it actually become the right time?", the compounding-cost argument, and "what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled?" The travel objection was never fully closed and the follow-up was booked on the far side of the trip.

Script gap, and the one that actually decided this call. The real blocker was not money — he had disclosed the capacity — it was provider trust: "I just have to see like how credited you are", "I need to do like more research", "I just have to see like the website, all the reviews and everything." The playbook has no due-diligence or credibility play, and the improvisation went the wrong way: the rep told him he would not get back in touch and was looking for an easy way out, then argued that anything he found online could be fake, testimonials included. Nothing verifiable was offered. Recording this as a script gap rather than a rep failure on the first half, and as a rep failure on the second.

notes: Best-executed process in the batch — the setter read-back, the baseline, the reflect-back and the full open-wallet picture are all things the rest of the corpus should be measured against — and it still lost the room, because the objection that mattered was trust and the response to it was pressure. Two coaching points: run P5 (four calls, zero consequence frames), and when a prospect asks for verification, give him verification. Separately and more seriously, the prospect disclosed active testosterone therapy and the response was to argue against it rather than to ask who prescribed it or whether he is cleared to train.
